title: structured-output: constrained decoding backends - tokenizer unicode + regex fallback improvements
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: Improve constrained-decoding backends used by structured output to handle tokenizer Unicode edge-cases and provide robust regex fallbacks when CFG constraints are not directly satisfiable by token boundaries.
Motivation: Customers hit correctness regressions when structured-output decoders produced invalid JSON or failed to match user-provided regex constraints due to multi-byte unicode token splits and tokenizer-dependent boundary decisions. This PR stabilizes the decoding backends by:
- Adding a tokenizer-aware Unicode re-joiner that attempts safe buffer merges across token boundaries when matching CFG terminals or regex anchors.
- Introducing a regex-fallback path that applies a byte/character-level match strategy when token-level greedy constraints would dead-end.
- Tightening loop invariants and timeouts in the constrained search to avoid pathological exponential search on long regex patterns.
- Exposing a small compatibility shim in the OpenAI-compat layer so existing integrations get the fallback behavior opt-in via a request flag.
Checklist:
- [x] Add tokenizer re-joiner logic and tests
- [x] Implement regex-fallback path with prioritization heuristics
- [x] Add end-to-end tests for JSON/CFG examples with multi-byte characters (emoji, accented characters, CJK)
- [x] Update OpenAI compatibility codepath and docs
- [x] Run perf benchmark suite and tune heuristics
- [x] Add e2e integration tests for streaming + constrained decoding
Changes (high-level):
- runtime/decoding/constrained_search.rs: Add TokenRejoiner, unicode-aware boundary heuristics, and fallback matcher hooks.
- runtime/decoding/regex_fallback.rs: New module implementing permissive character-level regex match and prioritized backtracking budget.
- openai-compat/handlers/structured_output.rs: Add opt-in header X-RW-Structured-Fallback and mapping to runtime flag.
- python-sdk/redwood/structured.py: Expose option "regex_fallback": bool for StructuredOutputRequest.
- tests/e2e/structured_unicode.py: End-to-end tests covering emoji, combining marks, and CJK.
- docs/api/structured-output.md: Document compatibility flag and recommended usage patterns.
Commits summary:
- 3c9f8d9 Add TokenRejoiner and tests for emoji boundaries
- 7b4a120 Implement regex fallback matcher with budgeted backtracking
- d2f1b6a OpenAI compat opt-in header + sdk flag
- e9a12b0 Performance tuning: reduce fallback budget when seq_len > 1024
- f3b4d21 Add e2e tests and docs
Update notes: The tokenizer rejoiner is conservative by default; it prefers token-preserving matches and only attempts character-level rejoin when CFG/regex fail at token boundaries. The regex fallback has a configurable budget (default tuned in this PR) to limit worst-case CPU.
Review conversation (summary):
- Liam: Asked for clarification on fallback priority vs. KV-cache reuse. Response: rejoiner only runs after cache-compatible token continuations are considered; added unit to prove cache safety and a comment in code.
- Priya: Requested additional tests for streaming partial-chunk scenarios. Response: added tests in tests/e2e/streaming_structured.py; verified streaming chunk boundaries now correctly propagate rejoin decisions without double-emitting tokens.
- Jordan: Flagged potential perf regression on long sequences; I ran the perf-canary suite and tuned the fallback budget; added a feature-flag to disable fallback for Dedicated plans if required.
CI and validation:
- Initial run: lint (pass), unit tests (fail on tokenizer edge-cases), integration tests (fail on one JSON streaming scenario).
- Follow-up run after fixes: all checks passed (unit+integration+e2e).
Perf benchmarks: modest overhead (3-7% CPU) on worst-case pathological inputs; typical workloads show negligible change and fewer structured-output retries.
Compatibility and migration:
- New behavior is opt-in via request flag X-RW-Structured-Fallback or StructuredOutputRequest(regex_fallback=True) in SDKs.
- Default behavior remains token-level constrained decoding to preserve deterministic costs.
- Release notes drafted in docs/api/structured-output.md.
Release notes: "Improved structured-output constrained decoding: better handling of Unicode tokenizer edge-cases and safer regex fallbacks. Opt-in compatibility flag available for gradual rollout. See docs/api/structured-output.md for migration guidance."

Risk and mitigation: The main risk is increased CPU on adversarial regexes; mitigations: budget limit, opt-in flag, Dedicated plans can turn off fallback.
Post-merge actions:
- Monitor canary metrics (structured-output error rate, CPU delta) for 72h
- Add telemetry event when fallback path is used (done in this PR)
- Schedule follow-up to consider auto-detection heuristics (ENG-4530)
